54.7: For, from all adversity He delivered me, And on my enemies has my eye looked!

55.1: To the Overseer with stringed instruments. --An instruction, by David. Give ear, O God, to my prayer, And hide not from my supplication.
55.2: Attend to me, and answer me, I mourn in my meditation, and make a noise,
55.3: Because of the voice of an enemy, Because of the oppression of the wicked, For they cause sorrow to move against me, And in anger they hate me.
55.4: My heart is pained within me, And terrors of death have fallen on me.
55.5: Fear and trembling come in to me, And horror does cover me.
55.6: And I say, `Who does give to me a pinion as a dove? I fly away and rest,
55.7: Indeed, I move far off, I lodge in a wilderness. Selah.
55.8: I hasten escape for myself, From a rushing wind, from a whirlwind.
55.9: Swallow up, O Lord, divide their tongue, For I saw violence and strife in a city.
55.10: By day and by night they go round it, on its walls. Both iniquity and perverseness are in its midst,
55.11: Mischiefs are in its midst. Fraud and deceit depart not from its street.
55.12: For an enemy reproaches me not, or I bear it, He who is hating me Has not magnified himself against me, Or I hide from him.
55.13: But you, a man--as my equal, My familiar friend, and my acquaintance.
55.14: When together we sweeten counsel, Into the house of God we walk in company.
55.15: Desolations are upon them, They go down to Sheol--alive, For wickedness is in their dwelling, in their midst.
55.16: I--to God I call, and Jehovah saves me.
55.17: Evening, and morning, and noon, I meditate, and make a noise, and He hears my voice,
55.18: He has ransomed in peace my soul From him who is near to me, For with the multitude they were with me.
55.19: God does hear and afflict them, And He sits of old. Selah. Because they have no changes, and fear not God,
55.20: He has sent forth his hands against his well-wishers, He has polluted his covenant.
55.21: Sweeter than honey has been his mouth, And his heart is war! Softer have been his words than oil, And they are drawn swords.
55.22: Cast on Jehovah that which He has given you, And He does sustain you, He does not suffer for ever the moving of the righteous.
55.23: And You, O God, do bring them down To a pit of destruction, Men of blood and deceit reach not to half their days, And I--I do trust in You!

56.1: To the Overseer. --`On the Dumb Dove far off.' --A secret treasure of David, in the Philistines' taking hold of him in Gath. Favour me, O God, for man swallowed me up, All the day fighting he oppresses me,
56.2: My enemies have swallowed up all the day, For many are fighting against me, O most High,
56.3: The day I am afraid I am confident toward You.
56.4: In God I praise His word, in God I have trusted, I fear not what flesh does to me.
56.5: All the day they wrest my words, Concerning me all their thoughts are for evil,
56.6: They assemble, they hide, they watch my heels, When they have expected my soul.
56.7: By iniquity they escape, In anger the peoples put down, O God.
56.8: My wandering You have counted, You--place You my tear in Your bottle, Are they not in Your book?
56.9: Then turn back do my enemies in the day I call. This I have known, that God is for me.
56.10: In God I praise the word, In Jehovah I praise the word.
56.11: In God I trusted, I fear not what man does to me,
56.12: On me, O God, are Your vows, I repay thank-offerings to You.
56.13: For You have delivered my soul from death, Do You not my feet from falling? To walk habitually before God in the light of the living!

57.1: To the Overseer. --`Destroy not.' --A secret treasure of David, in his fleeing from the face of Saul into a cave. Favour me, O God, favour me, For in You is my soul trusting, And in the shadow of Your wings I trust, Until the calamities pass over.
57.2: I call to God Most High, To God who is perfecting for me.
57.3: He sends from the heaven, and saves me, He reproached--who is panting after me. Selah. God sends forth His kindness and His truth.
57.4: My soul is in the midst of lions, I lie down among flames--sons of men, Their teeth are a spear and arrows, And their tongue a sharp sword.
57.5: Be You exalted above the heavens, O God, Above all the earth Your honour.
57.6: A net they have prepared for my steps, Bowed down has my soul, They have digged before me a pit, They have fallen into its midst. Selah.
57.7: Prepared is my heart, O God, Prepared is my heart, I sing and praise.
57.8: Awake, my honour, awake, psaltery and harp, I awake the morning dawn.
57.9: I thank You among the peoples, O Lord, I praise You among the nations.
57.10: For great to the heavens is Your kindness, And to the clouds Your truth.
57.11: Be you exalted above the heavens, O God. Above all the earth Your honour!

58.1: To the Overseer. --`Destroy not.' --A secret treasure, by David. Is it true, O dumb one, righteously you speak? Uprightly you judge, O sons of men?
58.2: Even in heart you work iniquities, In the land the violence of your hands you ponder.
58.3: The wicked have been estranged from the womb, They have erred from the belly, speaking lies.
58.4: Their poison is as poison of a serpent, As a deaf asp shutting its ear,
58.5: Which hearkens not to the voice of whisperers, A charmer of charms most skilful.
58.6: O God, break their teeth in their mouth, The jaw-teeth of young lions break down, O Jehovah.
58.7: They are melted as waters, They go up and down for themselves, His arrow proceeds as they cut themselves off.
58.8: As a snail that melts he goes on, As an untimely birth of a woman, They have not seen the sun.
58.9: Before your pots discern the bramble, As well the raw as the heated He whirls away.
58.10: The righteous rejoices that he has seen vengeance, His steps he washes in the blood of the wicked.
58.11: And man says: `Surely fruit is for the righteous: Surely there is a God judging in the earth!'

59.1: To the Overseer. --`Destroy not,' by David. --A secret treasure, in Saul's sending, and they watch the house to put him to death. Deliver me from my enemies, O my God, From my withstanders set me on high.
59.2: Deliver me from workers of iniquity, And from men of blood save me.
59.3: For, indeed, they laid wait for my soul, Assembled against me are strong ones, Not my transgression nor my sin, O Jehovah.
59.4: Without punishment they run and prepare themselves, Stir up to meet me, and see.
59.5: And You, Jehovah, God of Hosts, God of Israel, Awake to inspect all the nations. Favour not any treacherous dealers of iniquity. Selah.
59.6: They turn back at evening, They make a noise like a dog, And go round about the city.
59.7: Indeed, they belch out with their mouths, Swords are in their lips, for `Who hears?'
59.8: And You, O Jehovah do laugh at them, You do mock at all the nations.
59.9: O my Strength, to You I take heed, For God is my tower--the God of my kindness.
59.10: God does go before me, He causes me to look on my enemies.
59.11: Slay them not, lest my people forget, Shake them by Your strength, And bring them down, O Lord our shield.
59.12: The sin of their mouth is a word of their lips, And they are captured in their pride, And from the curse and lying they recount.
59.13: Consume in fury, consume and they are not, And they know that God is ruling in Jacob, To the ends of the earth. Selah.
59.14: And they turn back at evening, They make a noise like a dog, And they go round about the city.
59.15: They--they wander for food, If they are not satisfied--then they murmur.
59.16: And I--I sing of Your strength, And I sing at morn of Your kindness, For you have been a tower to me, And a refuge for me in a day of adversity.
59.17: O my Strength, to You I sing praise, For God is my tower, the God of my kindness!

60.1: To the Overseer. --`Concerning the Lily of Testimony,' a secret treasure of David, to teach, in his striving with Aram-Naharaim, and with Aram-Zobah, and Joab turns back and smites Edom in the valley of Salt--twelve thousand. O God, You had cast us off, You had broken us--had been angry! --You do turn back to us.
60.2: You have caused the land to tremble, You have broken it, Heal its breaches, for it has moved.
60.3: You have shown Your people a hard thing, You have caused us to drink wine of trembling.
60.4: You have given to those fearing you an ensign. To be lifted up as an ensign Because of truth. Selah.
60.5: That Your beloved ones may be drawn out, Save with Your right hand, and answer us.
60.6: God has spoken in His holiness: I exult--I apportion Shechem, And the valley of Succoth I measure,
60.7: Mine is Gilead, and mine is Manasseh, And Ephraim is the strength of my head, Judah is my lawgiver,
60.8: Moab is my pot for washing, over Edom I cast my shoe, Shout, concerning me, O Philistia.
60.9: Who does bring me to a city of bulwarks? Who has led me to Edom?
60.10: Is it not You, O God? have You cast us off? And do You not go forth, O God, with our hosts!
60.11: Give to us help from adversity, And vain is the deliverance of man.
60.12: In God we do mightily, And He treads down our adversaries!

61.1: To the Overseer, on stringed instruments. --By David. Hear, O God, my loud cry, attend to my prayer.
61.2: From the end of the land to You I call, In the feebleness of my heart, Into a rock higher than I You do lead me.
61.3: For You have been a refuge for me, A tower of strength because of the enemy.
61.4: I sojourn in Your tent to the ages, I trust in the secret place of Your wings. Selah.
61.5: For You, O God, have hearkened to my vows, You have appointed the inheritance Of those fearing Your name.
61.6: Days to the days of the king You add, His years as generation and generation.
61.7: He dwells to the age before God, Kindness and truth appoint--they keep him.
61.8: So do I praise Your name for ever, When I pay my vows day by day!

62.1: To the Overseer, for Jeduthun. --A Psalm of David. Only--toward God is my soul silent, From Him is my salvation.
62.2: Only--He is my rock, and my salvation, My tower, I am not much moved.
62.3: Till when do you devise mischief against a man? You are destroyed all of you, As a wall inclined, a hedge that is cast down.
62.4: Only--from his excellency They have consulted to drive away, They enjoy a lie, with their mouth they bless, And with their heart revile. Selah.
62.5: Only--for God, be silent, O my soul, For from Him is my hope.
62.6: Only--He is my rock and my salvation, My tower, I am not moved.
62.7: On God is my salvation, and my honour, The rock of my strength, my refuge is in God.
62.8: Trust in Him at all times, O people, Pour forth before Him your heart, God is a refuge for us. Selah.
62.9: Only--vanity are the low, a lie the high. In balances to go up they than vanity are lighter.
62.10: Trust not in oppression, And in robbery become not vain, Wealth--when it increases--set not the heart.
62.11: Once has God spoken, twice I heard this, That `strength is with God.'
62.12: And with You, O Lord, is kindness, For You do recompense to each, According to his work!

63.1: A Psalm of David, in his being in the wilderness of Judah. O God, You are my God, earnestly do I seek You, Thirsted for You has my soul, Longed for You has my flesh, In a land dry and weary, without waters.
63.2: So in the sanctuary I have seen You, To behold Your strength and Your honour.
63.3: Because better is Your kindness than life, My lips do praise You.
63.4: So I bless You in my life, in Your name I lift up my hands.
63.5: As with milk and fatness is my soul satisfied, And with singing lips does my mouth praise.
63.6: If I have remembered You on my couch, In the watches--I meditate on You.
63.7: For You have been a help to me, And in the shadow of Your wings I sing.
63.8: Cleaved has my soul after You, On me has Your right hand taken hold.
63.9: And they who for desolation seek my soul, Go in to the lower parts of the earth.
63.10: They cause him to run on the edge of the sword, A portion for foxes they are.
63.11: And the king does rejoice in God, Boast himself does every one swearing by Him, But stopped is the mouth of those speaking lies!

64.1: To the Overseer. --A Psalm of David. Hear, O God, my voice, in my meditation, From the fear of an enemy You keep my life,
64.2: Hide me from the secret counsel of evil doers, From the tumult of workers of iniquity.
64.3: Who sharpened as a sword their tongue, They directed their arrow--a bitter word.
64.4: To shoot in secret places the perfect, Suddenly they shoot him, and fear not.
64.5: They strengthen for themselves an evil thing, They recount of the hiding of snares, They have said, `Who does look at it?'
64.6: They search out perverse things, `We perfected a searching search,' And the inward part of man, and the heart are deep.
64.7: And God does shoot them with an arrow, Sudden have been their wounds,
64.8: And they cause him to stumble, Against them is their own tongue, Every looker on them flees away.
64.9: And all men fear, and declare the work of God, And His deed they have considered wisely.
64.10: The righteous does rejoice in Jehovah, And has trusted in Him, And boast themselves do all the upright of heart!

65.1: To the Overseer. --A Psalm of David. A Song. To You, silence--praise, O God, is in Zion, And to You is a vow completed.
65.2: Hearer of prayer, to You all flesh comes.
65.3: Matters of iniquities were mightier than I, Our transgressions--You do cover them.
65.4: O the happiness of him whom You choose, And draw near, he inhabits Your courts, We are satisfied with the goodness of Your house, Your holy temple.
65.5: By fearful things in righteousness You answer us, O God of our salvation, The confidence of all far off ends of earth and sea.
65.6: Establishing mountains by His power, He has been girded with might,
65.7: Restraining the noise of seas, the noise of their billows, And the multitude of the peoples.
65.8: And the inhabitants of the uttermost parts From Your signs are afraid, The outgoings of morning and evening You cause to sing.
65.9: You have inspected the earth, and water it, You make it very rich, the rivulet of God is full of water, You prepare their corn, When thus You do prepare it,
65.10: Its ridges have been filled, Deepened has been its furrow, With showers You do soften it, Its springing up You bless.
65.11: You have crowned the year of Your goodness, And Your paths drop fatness.
65.12: Drop do the pastures of a wilderness, And joy of the heights You gird on.
65.13: Clothed have lambs the flock, And valleys are covered with corn, They shout--yes, they sing!

66.1: To the Overseer. --A Song, a Psalm. Shout you to God, all the earth.
66.2: Praise you the honour of His name, Make you honourable His praise.
66.3: Say to God, `How fearful are Your works, By the abundance of Your strength, Your enemies feign obedience to You.
66.4: All the earth do bow to You, They sing praise to You, they praise Your name.' Selah.
66.5: Come you, and see the works of God, Fearful acts toward the sons of men.
66.6: He has turned a sea to dry land, Through a river they pass over on foot, There do we rejoice in Him.
66.7: Ruling by His might to the age, His eyes among the nations do watch, The refractory exalt not themselves. Selah.
66.8: Bless, you peoples, our God, And sound the voice of His praise,
66.9: Who has placed our soul in life, And suffered not our feet to be moved.
66.10: For You have tried us, O God, You have refined us as the refining of silver.
66.11: You have brought us into a net, You have placed pressure on our loins.
66.12: You have caused man to ride at our head. We have entered into fire and into water, And You bring us out to a watered place.
66.13: I enter Your house with burnt-offerings, I complete to You my vows,
66.14: For opened were my lips, And my mouth spoke in my distress:
66.15: `Burnt-offerings of fatlings I offer to You, With perfume of rams, I prepare a bullock with he-goats.' Selah.
66.16: Come, hear, all you who fear God, And I recount what he did for my soul.
66.17: To Him with my mouth I have called, And exaltation is under my tongue.
66.18: Iniquity, if I have seen in my heart, The Lord does not hear.
66.19: But God has heard, He has attended to the voice of my prayer.
66.20: Blessed is God, Who has not turned aside my prayer, And His loving-kindness, from me!

67.1: To the Overseer, with stringed instruments. --A Psalm, a Song. God does favour us and bless us, Does cause His face to shine with us. Selah.
67.2: For the knowledge in earth of Your way, among all nations of Your salvation.
67.3: Praise You do peoples, O God, Praise You do peoples, all of them.
67.4: Rejoice and sing do nations, For You judge peoples uprightly, And peoples on earth comfort. Selah.
67.5: Confess You do peoples, O God, Confess You do peoples--all of them.
67.6: Earth has given her increase, God does bless us--our God,
67.7: God does bless us, and all ends of earth fear Him!

68.1: To the Overseer. --A Psalm, a song of David. Rise does God--scattered are His enemies! And those hating Him flee from His face.
68.2: As the driving away of smoke You drive away, As the melting of wax before fire, The wicked perish at the presence of God.
68.3: And the righteous rejoice, they exult before God, And they joy with gladness.
68.4: Sing you to God--praise His name, Raise up a highway for Him who is riding in deserts, In Jah is His name, and exult before Him.
68.5: Father of the fatherless, and judge of the widows, Is God in His holy habitation.
68.6: God--causing the lonely to dwell at home, Bringing out bound ones into prosperity, Only--the refractory have inhabited a dry place.
68.7: O God, in Your going forth before Your people, In Your stepping through the wilderness, Selah.
68.8: The earth has shaken, Yes, the heavens have dropped before God, This Sinai--before God, the God of Israel.
68.9: A shower of free-will gifts you shake out, O God. Your inheritance, when it has been weary, You have established it.
68.10: Your company have dwelt in it, You prepare in Your goodness for the poor, O God.
68.11: The Lord does give the saying, The female proclaimers are a numerous host.
68.12: Kings of hosts flee utterly away, And a female inhabitant of the house apportions spoil.
68.13: Though you do lie between two boundaries, Wings of a dove covered with silver, And her pinions with yellow gold.
68.14: When the Mighty spreads kings in it, It does snow in Salmon.
68.15: A hill of God is the hill of Bashan, A hill of heights is the hill of Bashan.
68.16: Why do you envy, O high hills, The hill God has desired for His seat? Jehovah also does tabernacle for ever.
68.17: The chariots of God are myriads, thousands of changes, The Lord is among them, in Sinai, in the sanctuary.
68.18: You have ascended on high, You have taken captive captivity, You have taken gifts for men, That even the refractory may rest, O Jah God.
68.19: Blessed is the Lord, day by day He lays on us. God Himself is our salvation. Selah.
68.20: God Himself is to us a God for deliverances, And Jehovah Lord has the outgoings of death.
68.21: Only--God does smite The head of His enemies, The hairy crown of a habitual walker in his guilt.
68.22: The Lord said: `From Bashan I bring back, I bring back from the depths of the sea.
68.23: So that you dash your foot in blood, In the blood of enemies--the tongue of Your dogs.'
68.24: They have seen Your goings, O God, Goings of my God, my king, in the sanctuary.
68.25: Singers have been before, Behind are players on instruments, In the midst virgins playing with timbrels.
68.26: In assemblies bless you God, The Lord--from the fountain of Israel.
68.27: There is little Benjamin their ruler, Heads of Judah their defence, Heads of Zebulun--heads of Naphtali.
68.28: Your God has commanded your strength, Be strong, O God, this You have worked for us.
68.29: Because of Your temple at Jerusalem, To You do kings bring a present.
68.30: Rebuke a beast of the reeds, a company of bulls, With calves of the peoples, Each humbling himself with pieces of silver, Scatter You peoples delighting in conflicts.
68.31: Come do fat ones out of Egypt, Cush causes her hands to run to God.
68.32: Kingdoms of the earth, sing you to God, Praise you the Lord. Selah.
68.33: To him who is riding on the heavens of the heavens of old, Indeed, He gives with His voice a strong voice.
68.34: Ascribe you strength to God, Over Israel is His excellency, and His strength in the clouds.
68.35: Fearful, O God, out of Your sanctuaries, The God of Israel Himself, Giving strength and might to the people. Blessed is God!

69.1: To the Overseer. --`On the Lilies,' by David. Save me, O God, for come have waters to the soul.
69.2: I have sunk in deep mire, And there is no standing, I have come into the depths of the waters, And a flood has overflown me.
69.3: I have been wearied with my calling, Burnt has been my throat, Consumed have been my eyes, waiting for my God.
69.4: Those hating me without cause Have been more than the hairs of my head, Mighty have been my destroyers, My lying enemies, That which I took not away--I bring back.
69.5: O God, You--You have known Concerning my overturn, And my desolations from You have not been hid.
69.6: Let not those waiting on You be ashamed because of me, O Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, Let not those seeking You Blush because of me, O God of Israel.
69.7: For because of You I have borne reproach, Shame has covered my face.
69.8: A stranger I have been to my brother, And a foreigner to sons of my mother.
69.9: For zeal for Your house has consumed me, And the reproaches of Your reproachers Have fallen upon me.
69.10: And I weep in the fasting of my soul, And it is for a reproach to me.
69.11: And I make my clothing sackcloth, And I am to them for a simile.
69.12: Those sitting at the gate meditate concerning me, And those drinking strong drink, Play on instruments.
69.13: And I--my prayer is to You, O Jehovah, A time of good pleasure, O God, In the abundance of Your kindness, Answer me in the truth of Your salvation.
69.14: Deliver me from the mire, and let me not sink, Let me be delivered from those hating me, And from deep places of waters.
69.15: Let not a flood of waters overflow me, Nor let the deep swallow me up, Nor let the pit shut her mouth upon me.
69.16: Answer me, O Jehovah, for good is Your kindness, According to the abundance Of Your mercies turn You to me,
69.17: And hide not Your face from Your servant, For I am in distress--haste, answer me.
69.18: Be near to my soul--redeem it, Because of my enemies ransom me.
69.19: You--You have known my reproach, And my shame, and my blushing, Before You are all my adversaries.
69.20: Reproach has broken my heart, and I am sick, And I look for a bemoaner, and there is none, And for comforters, and I have found none.
69.21: And they give for my food gall, And for my thirst cause me to drink vinegar.
69.22: Their table before them is for a snare, And for a recompence--for a trap.
69.23: Darkened are their eyes from seeing, And their loins continually shake You.
69.24: Pour upon them Your indignation, And the fierceness of Your anger does seize them.
69.25: Their tower is desolated, In their tents there is no dweller.
69.26: For they have pursued him You have smitten, And recount of the pain of Your pierced ones.
69.27: Give punishment for their iniquity, And they enter not into Your righteousness.
69.28: They are blotted out of the book of life, And with the righteous are not written.
69.29: And I am afflicted and pained, Your salvation, O God, does set me on high.
69.30: I praise the name of God with a song, And I magnify Him with thanksgiving,
69.31: And it is better to Jehovah than an ox, A bullock--horned--hoofed.
69.32: The humble have seen--they rejoice, You who seek God--and your heart lives.
69.33: For Jehovah hearkens to the needy, And His bound ones He has not despised.
69.34: The heavens and earth do praise Him, Seas, and every moving thing in them.
69.35: For God does save Zion, And does build the cities of Judah, And they have dwelt there, and possess it.
69.36: And the seed of His servants inherit it, And those loving His name dwell in it!

70.1: To the Overseer, by David. --`To cause to remember.' O God, to deliver me, O Jehovah, for my help, haste.
70.2: Let them be ashamed and confounded Who are seeking my soul, Let them be turned backward and blush Who are desiring my evil.
70.3: Let them turn back because of their shame, Who are saying, `Aha, aha.'
70.4: Let all those seeking You joy and be glad in You, And let those loving Your salvation Say continually, `God is magnified.'
70.5: And I am poor and needy, O God, haste to me, My help and my deliverer are You, O Jehovah, tarry You not!

71.1: In You, O Jehovah, I have trusted, Let me not be ashamed to the age.
71.2: In Your righteousness You do deliver me, And do cause me to escape, Incline to me Your ear, and save me.
71.3: Be to me for a rock--a habitation, To go in continually, You have given command to save me, For my rock and my bulwark are You.
71.4: O my God, cause me to escape From the hand of the wicked, From the hand of the perverse and violent.
71.5: For You are my hope, O Lord Jehovah, My trust from my youth.
71.6: By You I have been supported from the womb, From my mother's bowels You do cut me out, In You is my praise continually.
71.7: As a wonder I have been to many, And You are my strong refuge.
71.8: Filled is my mouth with Your praise, All the day with Your beauty.
71.9: Cast me not off at the time of old age, According to the consumption of my power forsake me not.
71.10: For my enemies have spoken against me, And those watching my soul have taken counsel together,
71.11: Saying, `God has forsaken him, Pursue and catch him, for there is no deliverer.'
71.12: O God, be not far from me, O my God, for my help make haste.
71.13: They are ashamed, they are consumed, Who are opposing my soul, They are covered with reproach and blushing, Who are seeking my evil,
71.14: And I continually do wait with hope, And have added to all Your praise.
71.15: My mouth recounts Your righteousness, All the day Your salvation, For I have not known the numbers.
71.16: I come in the might of the Lord Jehovah, I mention Your righteousness--Your only.
71.17: God, You have taught me from my youth, And hitherto I declare Your wonders.
71.18: And also to old age and grey hairs, O God, forsake me not, Till I declare Your strength to a generation, To every one that comes Your might.
71.19: And Your righteousness, O God, is to the heights, Because You have done great things, O God, who is like You?
71.20: Because You have showed me many and sad distresses, You turn back--You revive me, And from the depths of the earth, You turn back--You bring me up.
71.21: You do increase my greatness, And You surround--You comfort me,
71.22: I also thank You with a vessel of psaltery, Your truth, O my God, I sing to You with a harp, O Holy One of Israel,
71.23: My lips cry aloud when I sing praise to You, And my soul that You have redeemed,
71.24: My tongue also all the day utters Your righteousness, Because ashamed--because confounded, Have been those seeking my evil!

72.1: By Solomon. O God, Your judgments to the king give, And Your righteousness to the king's son.
72.2: He judges Your people with righteousness, And Your poor with judgment.
72.3: The mountains bear peace to the people, And the heights by righteousness.
72.4: He judges the poor of the people, Gives deliverance to the sons of the needy, And bruises the oppressor.
72.5: They fear You with the sun, and before the moon, Generation--generations.
72.6: He comes down as rain on mown grass, As showers--sprinkling the earth.
72.7: Flourish in his days does the righteous, And abundance of peace till the moon is not.
72.8: And he rules from sea to sea, And from the river to the ends of earth.
72.9: Before him bow do the inhabitants of the dry places, And his enemies lick the dust.
72.10: Kings of Tarshish and of the isles send back a present. Kings of Sheba and Seba a reward bring near.
72.11: And all kings do bow themselves to him, All nations do serve him,
72.12: For he delivers the needy who cries, And the poor when he has no helper,
72.13: He has pity on the poor and needy, And the souls of the needy he saves,
72.14: From fraud and from violence he redeems their soul, And precious is their blood in his eyes.
72.15: And he lives, and gives to him of the gold of Sheba, And prays for him continually, All the day he does bless him.
72.16: There is a handful of corn in the earth, On the top of mountains, Shake like Lebanon does its fruit, And they flourish out of the city as the herb of the earth.
72.17: His name is to the age, Before the sun is his name continued, And they bless themselves in him, All nations do pronounce him happy.
72.18: Blessed is Jehovah God, God of Israel, He alone is doing wonders,
72.19: And blessed is the Name of His honour to the age, And the whole earth is filled with His honour. Amen, and amen!
72.20: The prayers of David son of Jesse have been ended.

73.1: A Psalm of Asaph. Only--good to Israel is God, to the clean of heart. And I--as a little thing, My feet have been turned aside,
73.2: As nothing, have my steps slipped, For I have been envious of the boastful,
73.3: The peace of the wicked I see, That there are no bands at their death,
73.5: In the misery of mortals they are not, And with common men they are not plagued.
73.6: Therefore has pride encircled them, Violence covers them as a dress.
73.7: Their eye has come out from fat. The imaginations of the heart transgressed;
73.8: They do corruptly, And they speak in the wickedness of oppression, From on high they speak.
73.9: They have set in the heavens their mouth, And their tongue walks in the earth.
73.10: Therefore do His people return here, And waters of fulness are wrung out to them.
73.11: And they have said, `How has God known? And is there knowledge in the Most High?'
73.12: Indeed, these are the wicked and easy ones of the age, They have increased strength.
73.13: Only--a vain thing! I have purified my heart, And I wash in innocency my hands,
73.14: And I am plagued all the day, And my reproof is every morning.
73.15: If I have said, `I recount thus,' Indeed, a generation of Your sons I have deceived.
73.16: And I think to know this, Perverseness it is in my eyes,
73.17: Till I come in to the sanctuaries of God, I attend to their latter end.
73.18: Only, in slippery places You do set them, You have caused them to fall to desolations.
73.19: How have they become a desolation as in a moment, They have been ended--consumed from terrors.
73.20: As a dream from awakening, O Lord, In awaking, their image You despise.
73.21: For my heart does show itself violent, And my reins prick themselves,
73.22: And I am brutish, and do not know. A beast I have been with You.
73.23: And I am continually with You, You have laid hold on my right hand.
73.24: With Your counsel You do lead me, And after honour do receive me.
73.25: Whom have I in the heavens? And with You none I have desired in earth.
73.26: Consumed has been my flesh and my heart, The rock of my heart and my portion is God to the age.
73.27: For, indeed, those far from You do perish, You have cut off every one, Who is going a whoring from You.
73.28: And I--nearness of God to me is good, I have placed in the Lord Jehovah my refuge, To recount all Your works!

74.1: An Instruction of Asaph. Why, O God, have You cast off for ever? Your anger smokes against the flock of Your pasture.
74.2: Remember Your company. You did purchase of old, You did redeem the rod of Your inheritance, This mount Zion--You did dwell in it.
74.3: Lift up Your steps to the perpetual desolations, Everything the enemy did wickedly in the sanctuary.
74.4: Roared have your adversaries, In the midst of Your meeting-places, They have set their ensigns as ensigns.
74.5: He is known as one bringing in on high Against a thicket of wood--axes.
74.6: And now, its carvings together With axe and hatchet they break down,
74.7: They have sent into fire Your sanctuary, to the earth they polluted the tabernacle of Your name,
74.8: They said in their hearts, `Let us oppress them together,' They did burn all the meeting-places of God in the land.
74.9: Our ensigns we have not seen, There is no more a prophet, Nor with us is one knowing how long.
74.10: Till when, O God, does an adversary reproach? Does an enemy despise your name for ever?
74.11: Why do You turn back Your hand, Even Your right hand? From the midst of Your bosom remove it.
74.12: And God is my king of old, Working salvation in the midst of the earth.
74.13: You have broken by Your strength a sea- monster, You have shivered Heads of dragons by the waters,
74.14: You have broken the heads of leviathan, You make him food, For the people of the dry places.
74.15: You have cleaved a fountain and a stream, You have dried up perennial flowings.
74.16: Yours is the day, also Yours is the night, You have prepared a light giver--the sun.
74.17: You have set up all the borders of earth, Summer and winter You have formed them.
74.18: Remember this--an enemy reproached Jehovah, And a foolish people have despised Your name.
74.19: Give not up to a company, The soul of Your turtle-dove, The company of Your poor ones forget not for ever.
74.20: Look attentively to the covenant, For the dark places of earth, Have been full of habitations of violence.
74.21: Let not the oppressed turn back ashamed, Let the poor and needy praise Your name,
74.22: Arise, O God, plead Your plea, Remember Your reproach from a fool all the day.
74.23: Forget not the voice of Your adversaries, The noise of Your withstanders is going up continually!

75.1: To the Overseer. --`Destroy not.' --A Psalm of Asaph. --A Song. We have given thanks to You, O God, We have given thanks, and near is Your name, They have recounted Your wonders.
75.2: When I receive an appointment, I--I do judge uprightly.
75.3: Melted is the earth and all its inhabitants, I--I have pondered its pillars. Selah.
75.4: I have said to the boastful, `Be not boastful,' And to the wicked, `Raise not up a horn.'
75.5: Raise not up on high your horn, (You speak with a stiff neck.)
75.6: For not from the east, or from the west, Nor from the wilderness-- is elevation.
75.7: But God is judge, This He makes low--and this He lifts up.
75.8: For a cup is in the hand of Jehovah, And the wine has foamed, It is full of mixture, and He pours out of it, Only its dregs wring out, and drink, Do all the wicked of the earth,
75.9: And I--I declare it to the age, I sing praise to the God of Jacob.
75.10: And all horns of the wicked I cut off, Exalted are the horns of the righteous!

76.1: To the Overseer with stringed instruments. --A Psalm of Asaph. --A Song. In Judah is God known, in Israel His name is great.
76.2: And His tabernacle is in Salem, And His habitation in Zion.
76.3: There he has shivered arrows of a bow, Shield, and sword, and battle. Selah.
76.4: Bright are You, honourable above hills of prey.
76.5: Spoiled themselves have the mighty of heart, They have slept their sleep, And none of the men of might found their hands.
76.6: From Your rebuke, O God of Jacob, Both rider and horse have been fast asleep.
76.7: You, fearful are You, And who does stand before You, Since You have been angry!
76.8: From heaven You have sounded judgment, Earth has feared, and has been still,
76.9: In the rising of God to judgment, To save all the humble of earth. Selah.
76.10: For the fierceness of man praises You, The remnant of fierceness You gird on.
76.11: Vow and complete to Jehovah your God, All you surrounding him. They bring presents to the Fearful One.
76.12: He does gather the spirit of leaders, Fearful to the kings of earth!

77.1: To the Overseer, for Jeduthun. --A Psalm of Asaph. My voice is to God, and I cry, my voice is to God, And He has given ear to me.
77.2: In a day of my distress the Lord I sought, My hand by night has been spread out, And it does not cease, My soul has refused to be comforted.
77.3: I remember God, and make a noise, I meditate, and feeble is my spirit. Selah.
77.4: You have taken hold of the watches of my eyes, I have been moved, and I speak not.
77.5: I have reckoned the days of old, The years of the ages.
77.6: I remember my music in the night, With my heart I meditate, and my spirit does search diligently:
77.7: To the ages does the Lord cast off? Does He add to be pleased no more?
77.8: Has His kindness ceased for ever? The saying failed to all generations?
77.9: Has God forgotten His favours? Has He shut up in anger His mercies? Selah.
77.10: And I say: `My weakness is, The changes of the right hand of the Most High.'
77.11: I mention the doings of Jah, For I remember of old Your wonders,
77.12: And I have meditated on all Your working, And I talk concerning Your doings.
77.13: O God, in holiness is Your way, Who is a great god like God?
77.14: You are the God doing wonders. You have made known among the peoples Your strength,
77.15: You have redeemed with strength Your people, The sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
77.16: The waters have seen You, O God, The waters have seen You, They are afraid--also depths are troubled.
77.17: Poured out waters have thick clouds, The skies have given forth a noise, Also--Your arrows go up and down.
77.18: The voice of Your thunder is in the spheres, Lightnings have lightened the world, The earth has trembled, yes, it shakes.
77.19: In the sea is Your way, And Your paths are in many waters, And Your tracks have not been known.
77.20: You have led as a flock Your people, By the hand of Moses and Aaron!

78.1: An Instruction of Asaph. Give ear, O my people, to my law, Incline your ear to sayings of my mouth.
78.2: I open with a simile my mouth, I bring forth hidden things of old,
78.3: That we have heard and do know, And our fathers have recounted to us.
78.4: We do not hide from their sons, To a later generation recounting praises of Jehovah, And His strength, and His wonders that He has done.
78.5: And He raises up a testimony in Jacob, And a law has placed in Israel, That He commanded our fathers, To make them known to their sons.
78.6: So that a later generation does know, Sons who are born, do rise and recount to their sons,
78.7: And place in God their confidence, And forget not the doings of God, But keep His commands.
78.8: And they are not like their fathers, A generation apostate and rebellious, A generation! it has not prepared its heart, Nor stedfast with God is its spirit.
78.9: Sons of Ephraim--armed bearers of bow, Have turned in a day of conflict.
78.10: They have not kept the covenant of God, And in His law they have refused to walk,
78.11: And they forget His doings, And His wonders that He showed them.
78.12: Before their fathers He has done wonders, In the land of Egypt--the field of Zoan.
78.13: He cleft a sea, and causes them to pass over, Yes, He causes waters to stand as a heap.
78.14: And leads them with a cloud by day, And all the night with a light of fire.
78.15: He cleaves rocks in a wilderness, And gives drink--as the great deep.
78.16: And brings out streams from a rock, And causes waters to come down as rivers.
78.17: And they add still to sin against Him, To provoke the Most High in the dry place.
78.18: And they try God in their heart, To ask food for their lust.
78.19: And they speak against God--they said: `Is God able to array a table in a wilderness?'
78.20: Indeed, He has smitten a rock, And waters flow, yes, streams overflow. `Also--bread is He able to give? Does He prepare flesh for His people?'
78.21: Therefore has Jehovah heard, And He shows Himself wroth, And fire has been kindled against Jacob, And anger also has gone up against Israel,
78.22: For they have not believed in God, Nor have they trusted in His salvation.
78.23: And He commands clouds from above, Yes, doors of the heavens He has opened.
78.24: And He rains on them manna to eat, Yes, corn of heaven He has given to them.
78.25: Food of the mighty has each eaten, Venison He sent to them to satiety.
78.26: He causes an east wind to journey in the heavens, And leads by His strength a south wind,
78.27: And He rains on them flesh as dust, And as sand of the seas--winged fowl,
78.28: And causes it to fall in the midst of His camp, Round about His tabernacles.
78.29: And they eat, and are greatly satisfied, And their desire He brings to them.
78.30: They have not been estranged from their desire, Yet is their food in their mouth,
78.31: And the anger of God has gone up against them, And He slays among their fat ones, And youths of Israel He caused to bend.
78.32: With all this they have sinned again, And have not believed in His wonders.
78.33: And He consumes in vanity their days, And their years in trouble.
78.34: If He slew them, then they sought Him, And turned back, and sought God earnestly,
78.35: And they remember that God is their rock, And God Most High their redeemer.
78.36: And--they deceive Him with their mouth, And with their tongue do lie to Him,
78.37: And their heart has not been right with Him, And they have not been stedfast in His covenant.
78.38: And He--the Merciful One, Pardons iniquity, and destroys not, And has often turned back His anger, And wakes not up all His fury.
78.39: And He remembers that they are flesh, A wind going on--and it returns not.
78.40: How often do they provoke Him in the wilderness, Grieve Him in the desolate place?
78.41: Yes, they turn back, and try God, And the Holy One of Israel have limited.
78.42: They have not remembered His hand The day He ransomed them from the adversary.
78.43: When He set His signs in Egypt, And His wonders in the field of Zoan,
78.44: And He turns to blood their streams, And their floods they drink not.
78.45: He sends among them the beetle, and it consumes them, And the frog, and it destroys them,
78.46: And gives to the caterpillar their increase, And their labour to the locust.
78.47: He destroys with hail their vine, And their sycamores with frost,
78.48: And delivers up to the hail their beasts, And their cattle to the burning flames.
78.49: He sends on them the fury of His anger, Wrath, and indignation, and distress--A discharge of evil messengers.
78.50: He ponders a path for His anger, He kept not back their soul from death, Yes, their life to the pestilence He delivered up.
78.51: And He smites every first-born in Egypt, The first-fruit of the strong in tents of Ham.
78.52: And causes His people to journey as a flock, And guides them as a drove in a wilderness,
78.53: And He leads them confidently, And they have not been afraid, And their enemies has the sea covered.
78.54: And He brings them in to the border of His sanctuary, This mountain His right hand had got,
78.55: And casts out nations from before them, And causes them to fall in the line of inheritance, And causes the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents,
78.56: And they tempt and provoke God Most High, And His testimonies have not kept.
78.57: And they turn back, And deal treacherously like their fathers, They have been turned like a deceitful bow,
78.58: And make Him angry with their high places, And with their graven images make Him zealous,
78.59: God has heard, and shows Himself wroth. And kicks exceedingly against Israel.
78.60: And He leaves the tabernacle of Shiloh, The tent He had placed among men,
78.61: And He gives His strength to captivity, And His beauty into the hand of an adversary,
78.62: And delivers up to the sword His people, And with His inheritance showed Himself angry.
78.63: His young men has fire consumed, And His virgins have not been praised.
78.64: His priests by the sword have fallen, And their widows weep not.
78.65: And the Lord wakes as a sleeper, As a mighty one crying aloud from wine.
78.66: And He smites His adversaries backward, A reproach age-during He has put on them,
78.67: And He kicks against the tent of Joseph, And on the tribe of Ephraim has not fixed.
78.68: And He chooses the tribe of Judah, With mount Zion that He loved,
78.69: And builds His sanctuary as a high place, Like the earth, He founded it to the age.
78.70: And He fixes on David His servant, And takes him from the folds of a flock,
78.71: From behind suckling ones He has brought him in, To rule over Jacob His people, And over Israel His inheritance.
78.72: And he rules them according to the integrity of his heart, And by the skilfulness of his hands leads them!

79.1: A Psalm of Asaph. O God, nations have come into Your inheritance, They have defiled Your holy temple, They made Jerusalem become heaps,
79.2: They gave the dead bodies of Your servants Food for the fowls of the heavens, The flesh of Your saints For the wild beast of the earth.
79.3: They have shed their blood As water round about Jerusalem, And there is none burying.
79.4: We have been a reproach to our neighbours, A scorn and a derision to our surrounders.
79.5: Till when, O Jehovah? are You angry for ever? Your jealousy does burn as fire.
79.6: Pour Your fury on the nations who have not known You, And on kingdoms that have not called in Your name.
79.7: For one has devoured Jacob, And his habitation they have made desolate.
79.8: Remember not for us the iniquities of forefathers, Haste, let Your mercies go before us, For we have been very weak.
79.9: Help us, O God of our salvation, Because of the honour of Your name, And deliver us, and cover over our sins, For Your name's sake.
79.10: Why do the nations say, `Where is their God?' Let be known among the nations before our eyes, The vengeance of the blood of Your servants that is shed.
79.11: Let the groaning of the prisoner come in before You, According to the greatness of Your arm, Leave You the sons of death.
79.12: And turn You back to our neighbours, Sevenfold to their bosom, their reproach, With which they reproached You, O Lord.
79.13: And we, Your people, and the flock of Your pasture, We give thanks to You to the age, To all generations we recount Your praise!

80.1: To the Overseer. --`On the Lilies.' A testimony of Asaph. --A Psalm. Shepherd of Israel, give ear, Leading Joseph as a flock, Inhabiting the cherubs--shine forth,
80.2: Before Ephraim, and Benjamin, and Manasseh, Wake up Your might, and come for our salvation.
80.3: O God, cause us to turn back, And cause Your face to shine, and we are saved.
80.4: Jehovah, God of Hosts, till when? You have burned against the prayer of Your people.
80.5: You have caused them to eat bread of tears, And cause them to drink With tears a third time.
80.6: You make us a strife to our neighbours, And our enemies mock at it.
80.7: God of Hosts, turn us back, And cause Your face to shine, and we are saved.
80.8: A vine out of Egypt You do bring, You do cast out nations, and plant it.
80.9: You have looked before it, and do root it, And it fills the land,
80.10: Covered have been hills with its shadow, And its boughs are cedars of God.
80.11: It sends forth its branches to the sea, And to the river its sucklings.
80.12: Why have You broken down its hedges, And all passing by the way have plucked it?
80.13: A boar out of the forest does waste it, And a wild beast of the fields consumes it.
80.14: God of Hosts, turn back, we beseech You, Look from heaven, and see, and inspect this vine,
80.15: And the root that Your right hand planted, And the branch You made strong for You,
80.16: Burnt with fire--cut down, From the rebuke of Your face they perish.
80.17: Let Your hand be on the man of Your right hand, On the son of man You have strengthened for Yourself.
80.18: And we do not go back from You, You do revive us, and in Your name we call.
80.19: O Jehovah, God of Hosts, turn us back, Cause Your face to shine, and we are saved!

81.1: To the Overseer. --`On the Gittith.' By Asaph. Cry aloud to God our strength, Shout to the God of Jacob.
81.2: Lift up a song, and give out a timbrel, A pleasant harp with psaltery.
81.3: Blow in the month a trumpet, In the new moon, at the day of our festival,
81.4: For a statute to Israel it is, An ordinance of the God of Jacob.
81.5: A testimony on Joseph He has placed it, In his going forth over the land of Egypt. A lip, I have not known--I hear.
81.6: From the burden his shoulder I turned aside, His hands from the basket pass over.
81.7: In distress you have called and I deliver you, I answer you in the secret place of thunder, I try you by the waters of Meribah. Selah.
81.8: Hear, O My people, and I testify to you, O Israel, if you do hearken to me:
81.9: There is not in you a strange god, And you bow not yourself to a strange god.
81.10: I am Jehovah your God, Who brings you up out of the land of Egypt. Enlarge your mouth, and I fill it.
81.11: But, My people hearkened not to My voice, And Israel has not consented to Me.
81.12: And I send them away in the enmity of their heart, They walk in their own counsels.
81.13: O that My people were hearkening to Me, Israel in My ways would walk.
81.14: As a little thing their enemies I cause to bow, And against their adversaries I turn back My hand,
81.15: Those hating Jehovah feign obedience to Him, But their time is--to the age.
81.16: He causes him to eat of the fat of wheat, And with honey from a rock I satisfy you!

82.1: --A Psalm of Asaph. God has stood in the company of God, In the midst God does judge.
82.2: Till when do you judge perversely? And the face of the wicked lift up? Selah.
82.3: Judge you the weak and fatherless, The afflicted and the poor declare righteous.
82.4: Let the weak and needy escape, From the hand of the wicked deliver them.
82.5: They knew not, nor do they understand, In darkness they walk habitually, Moved are all the foundations of earth.
82.6: I--I have said, `Gods you are, And sons of the Most High--all of you,
82.7: But as man you die, and as one of the heads you fall,
82.8: Rise, O God, judge the earth, For You have inheritance among all the nations!

83.1: A Song, --A Psalm of Asaph. O God, let there be no silence to You, Be not silent, nor be quiet, O God.
83.2: For, indeed, Your enemies do roar, And those hating You have lifted up the head,
83.3: Against Your people they take crafty counsel, And consult against Your hidden ones.
83.4: They have said, `Come, And we cut them off from being a nation, And the name of Israel is not remembered any more.'
83.5: For they consulted in heart together, Against You a covenant they make,
83.6: Tents of Edom, and Ishmaelites, Moab, and the Hagarenes,
83.7: Gebal, and Ammon, and Amalek, Philistia with inhabitants of Tyre,
83.8: Asshur also is joined with them, They have been an arm to sons of Lot. Selah.
83.9: Do to them as to Midian, As to Sisera, as to Jabin, at the stream Kishon.
83.10: They were destroyed at Endor, They were dung for the ground!
83.11: Make their nobles as Oreb and as Zeeb, And as Zebah and Zalmunna all their princes,
83.12: Who have said, `Let us occupy for ourselves The comely places of God.'
83.13: O my God, make them as a rolling thing, As stubble before wind.
83.14: As a fire does burn a forest, And as a flame sets hills on fire,
83.15: So do You pursue them with Your whirlwind, And with Your hurricane trouble them.
83.16: Fill their faces with shame, And they seek Your name, O Jehovah.
83.17: They are ashamed and troubled for ever, Yes, they are confounded and lost.
83.18: And they know that You--(Your name is Jehovah--by Yourself,) Art the Most High over all the earth!

84.1: To the Overseer. --`On the Gittith By sons of Korah.' --A Psalm. How beloved Your tabernacles, Jehovah of Hosts!
84.2: My soul desired, yes, it has also been consumed, For the courts of Jehovah, My heart and my flesh cry aloud to the living God,
84.3: (Even a sparrow has found a house, And a swallow a nest for herself, Where she has placed her brood,) Your altars, O Jehovah of Hosts, My king and my God.
84.4: O the happiness of those inhabiting Your house, Yet do they praise You. Selah.
84.5: O the happiness of a man whose strength is in You, Highways are in their heart.
84.6: Those passing through a valley of weeping, A fountain do make it, Blessings also cover the director.
84.7: They go from strength to strength, He appears to God in Zion.
84.8: O Jehovah, God of Hosts, hear my prayer, Give ear, O God of Jacob. Selah.
84.9: Our shield, see, O God, And behold the face of Your anointed,
84.10: For good is a day in Your courts, O Teacher! I have chosen rather to be at the threshold, In the house of my God, Than to dwell in tents of wickedness.
84.11: For a sun and a shield is Jehovah God, Grace and honour does Jehovah give. He withholds not good To those walking in uprightness.
84.12: Jehovah of Hosts! O the happiness of a man trusting in You.

85.1: To the Overseer. --By sons of Korah. A Psalm. You have accepted, O Jehovah, Your land, You have turned to the captivity of Jacob.
85.2: You have borne away the iniquity of Your people, You have covered all their sin. Selah.
85.3: You have gathered up all Your wrath, You have turned back from the fierceness of Your anger.
85.4: Turn back to us, O God of our salvation, And make void Your anger with us.
85.5: To the age are You angry against us? Do You draw out Your anger To generation and generation?
85.6: Do You not turn back? You revive us, And Your people do rejoice in You.
85.7: Show us, O Jehovah, your kindness, And Your salvation You do give to us.
85.8: I hear what God Jehovah speaks, For He speaks peace to His people, And to His saints, and they turn not back to folly.
85.9: Only, near to those fearing Him is His salvation, That honour may dwell in our land.
85.10: Kindness and truth have met, Righteousness and peace have kissed,
85.11: Truth from the earth springs up, And righteousness from heaven looks out,
85.12: Jehovah also gives that which is good, And our land does give its increase.
85.13: Righteousness before Him goes, And makes His footsteps for a way!

86.1: A Prayer of David. Incline, O Jehovah, Your ear, Answer me, for I am poor and needy.
86.2: Keep my soul, for I am pious, Save Your servant--who is trusting to You, O You, my God.
86.3: Favour me, O Lord, for to You I call all the day.
86.4: Rejoice the soul of Your servant, For to You, O Lord, my soul I lift up.
86.5: For You, Lord, are good and forgiving. And abundant in kindness to all calling You.
86.6: Hear, O Jehovah, my prayer, And attend to the voice of my supplications.
86.7: In a day of my distress I call You, For You do answer me.
86.8: There is none like You among the gods, O Lord, And like Your works there are none.
86.9: All nations that You have made Come and bow themselves before You, O Lord, And give honour to Your name.
86.10: For great are You, and doing wonders, You are God Yourself alone.
86.11: Show me, O Jehovah, Your way, I walk in Your truth, My heart does rejoice to fear Your name.
86.12: I confess You, O Lord my God, with all my heart, And I honour Your name to the age.
86.13: For Your kindness is great toward me, And You have delivered my soul from the lowest Sheol.
86.14: O God, the proud have risen up against me, And a company of the terrible sought my soul, And have not placed You before them,
86.15: And You, O Lord, are God, merciful and gracious, Slow to anger, and abundant in kindness and truth.
86.16: Look to me, and favour me, Give Your strength to Your servant, And give salvation to a son of Your handmaid.
86.17: Do with me a sign for good, And those hating me see and are ashamed, For You, O Jehovah, have helped me, Yes, You have comforted me!

87.1: By sons of Korah. --A Psalm, a song. His foundation is in holy mountains.
87.2: Jehovah is loving the gates of Zion Above all the tabernacles of Jacob.
87.3: Honourable things are spoken in You, O city of God. Selah.
87.4: I mention Rahab and Babel to those knowing Me, Indeed, Philistia, and Tyre, with Cush! This one was born there.
87.5: And of Zion it is said: Each one was born in her, And He, the Most High, does establish her.
87.6: Jehovah does recount in the describing of the peoples, `This one was born there.' Selah.
87.7: Singers also as players on instruments, All my fountains are in You!

88.1: A Song, a Psalm, by sons of Korah, to the Overseer, `Concerning the Sickness of Afflictions.' --An instruction, by Heman the Ezrahite. O Jehovah, God of my salvation, Daily I have cried, nightly before You,
88.2: My prayer comes in before You, Incline Your ear to my loud cry,
88.3: For my soul has been full of evils, And my life has come to Sheol.
88.4: I have been reckoned with those going down to the pit, I have been as a man without strength.
88.5: Among the dead--free, As pierced ones lying in the grave, Whom You have not remembered any more, Yes, they by Your hand have been cut off.
88.6: You have put me in the lowest pit, In dark places, in depths.
88.7: Upon me has Your fury lain, And with all Your breakers You have afflicted. Selah.
88.8: You have put my acquaintance far from me, You have made me an abomination to them, Shut up--I go not forth.
88.9: My eye has grieved because of affliction, I called You, O Jehovah, all the day, I have spread out to You my hands.
88.10: To the dead do You do wonders? Do Rephaim rise? do they thank You? Selah.
88.11: Is Your kindness recounted in the grave? Your faithfulness in destruction?
88.12: Are Your wonders known in the darkness? And Your righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?
88.13: And I, to You, O Jehovah, I have cried, And in the morning does my prayer come before You.
88.14: Why, O Jehovah, cast You off my soul? You hide Your face from me.
88.15: I am afflicted, and expiring from youth, I have borne Your terrors--I pine away.
88.16: Over me has Your wrath passed, Your terrors have cut me off,
88.17: They have surrounded me as waters all the day, They have gone round against me together,
88.18: You have put far from me lover and friend, My acquaintance is the place of darkness!

89.1: An instruction, by Ethan the Ezrahite. Of the kind acts of Jehovah, to the age I sing, To all generations I make known Your faithfulness with my mouth,
89.2: For I said, `To the age is kindness built, The heavens! You do establish Your faithfulness in them.'
89.3: I have made a covenant for My chosen, I have sworn to David My servant:
89.4: `Even to the age do I establish your seed, And have built to generation and generation your throne. Selah.
89.5: and the heavens confess Your wonders, O Jehovah, Your faithfulness also is in an assembly of holy ones.
89.6: For who in the sky, Compares himself to Jehovah? Is like to Jehovah among sons of the mighty?
89.7: God is very terrible, In the secret counsel of His holy ones, And fearful over all surrounding Him.
89.8: O Jehovah, God of Hosts, Who is like You--a strong Jah? And Your faithfulness is round about You.
89.9: You are ruler over the pride of the sea, In the lifting up of its billows You do restrain them.
89.10: You have bruised Rahab, as one wounded. With the arm of Your strength You have scattered Your enemies.
89.11: Yours are the heavens--the earth also is Yours, The habitable world and its fulness, You have founded them.
89.12: North and south You have appointed them, Tabor and Hermon in Your name do sing.
89.13: You have an arm with might, Strong is Your hand--high Your right hand.
89.14: Righteousness and judgment Are the fixed place of Your throne, Kindness and truth go before Your face.
89.15: O the happiness of the people knowing the shout, O Jehovah, in the light of Your face they walk habitually.
89.16: In Your name they rejoice all the day, And in Your righteousness they are exalted,
89.17: For the beauty of their strength are You, And in Your good will is our horn exalted,
89.18: For of Jehovah is our shield, And of the Holy One of Israel our king.
89.19: Then You have spoken in vision, To Your saint, yes, You say, I have placed help upon a mighty one, Exalted a chosen one out of the people,
89.20: I have found David My servant, With My holy oil I have anointed him.
89.21: With whom My hand is established, My arm also does strengthen him.
89.22: An enemy exacts not upon him, And a son of perverseness afflicts him not.
89.23: And I have beaten down before him his adversaries, And those hating him I plague,
89.24: And My faithfulness and kindness are with him, And in My name is his horn exalted.
89.25: And I have set on the sea his hand, And on the rivers his right hand.
89.26: He proclaims me: `You are my Father, My God, and the rock of my salvation.'
89.27: I also first-born do appoint him, Highest of the kings of the earth.
89.28: To the age I keep for him My kindness, And My covenant is stedfast with him.
89.29: And I have set his seed for ever, And his throne as the days of the heavens.
89.30: If his sons forsake My law, And in My judgments do not walk;
89.31: If My statutes they pollute, And My commands do not keep,
89.32: I have looked after with a rod their transgression, And with strokes their iniquity,
89.33: And My kindness I break not from him, Nor do I deal falsely in My faithfulness.
89.34: I profane not My covenant, And that which is going forth from My lips I change not.
89.35: Once I have sworn by My holiness, I lie not to David,
89.36: His seed is to the age, And his throne is as the sun before Me,
89.37: As the moon it is established--to the age, And the witness in the sky is stedfast. Selah.
89.38: And You, You have cast off, and do reject, You have shown Yourself wroth With Your anointed,
89.39: Have rejected the covenant of Your servant, You have polluted to the earth his crown,
89.40: You have broken down all his hedges, You have made his fenced places a ruin.
89.41: Spoiled him have all passing by the way, He has been a reproach to his neighbours,
89.42: You have exalted the right hand of his adversaries, You have caused all his enemies to rejoice.
89.43: Also--You turn back the sharpness of his sword, And have not established him in battle,
89.44: Have caused him to cease from his brightness, And his throne to the earth have cast down.
89.45: You have shortened the days of his youth, Have covered him over with shame. Selah.
89.46: Till when, O Jehovah, are You hidden? For ever does Your fury burn as fire?
89.47: Remember, I pray You, what is life-time? Wherefore in vain have You created All the sons of men?
89.48: Who is the man that lives, and does not see death? He delivers his soul from the hand of Sheol. Selah.
89.49: Where are Your former kindnesses, O Lord. You have sworn to David in Your faithfulness,
89.50: Remember, O Lord, the reproach of Your servants, I have borne in my bosom all the strivings of the peoples,
89.51: With which Your enemies reproached, O Jehovah, With which they have reproached The steps of Your anointed.
89.52: Blessed is Jehovah to the age. Amen, and amen!

90.1: A Prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, a habitation You--You have been, To us--in generation and generation,
90.2: Before mountains were brought forth, And You do form the earth and the world, Even from age to age You are God.
90.3: You turn man to a bruised thing, And say, Turn back, you sons of men.
90.4: For a thousand years in Your eyes are as yesterday, For it passes on, yes, a watch by night.
90.5: You have inundated them, they are asleep, In the morning as grass he changes.
90.6: In the morning it flourishes, and has changed, At evening it is cut down, and has withered.
90.7: For we were consumed in Your anger, And in Your fury we have been troubled.
90.8: You have set our iniquities before You, Our hidden things at the light of Your face,
90.9: For all our days pined away in Your wrath, We consumed our years as a meditation.
90.10: Days of our years, in them are seventy years, And if, by reason of might, eighty years, Yet is their enlargement labour and vanity, For it has been cut off hastily, and we fly away.
90.11: Who knows the power of Your anger? And according to Your fear--Your wrath?
90.12: To number our days aright let us know, And we bring the heart to wisdom.
90.13: Turn back, O Jehovah, till when? And repent concerning Your servants.
90.14: Satisfy us at morn with Your kindness, And we sing and rejoice all our days.
90.15: Cause us to rejoice according to the days In which You have afflicted us, The years we have seen evil.
90.16: Let Your work appear to Your servants, And Your honour on their sons.
90.17: And let the pleasantness of Jehovah our God be upon us, And the work of our hands establish on us, Yes, the work of our hands establish it!

91.1: He who is dwelling In the secret place of the Most High, In the shade of the Mighty lodges habitually,
91.2: He is saying of Jehovah, `My refuge, and my bulwark, my God, I trust in Him,'
91.3: For He delivers you from the snare of a fowler, From a calamitous pestilence.
91.4: With His pinion He covers you over, And under His wings you do trust, A shield and buckler is His truth.
91.5: You are not afraid of fear by night, Of arrow that flies by day,
91.6: Of pestilence in thick darkness that walks, Of destruction that destroys at noon,
91.7: There fall at your side a thousand, And a myriad at your right hand, To you it comes not nigh.
91.8: But with your eyes you look, And the reward of the wicked you see,
91.9: (For You, O Jehovah, are my refuge,) The Most High you made your habitation.
91.10: Evil happens not to you, And a plague comes not near your tent,
91.11: For His messengers He charges for you, To keep you in all your ways,
91.12: On the hands they bear you up, Lest you smite against a stone your foot.
91.13: On lion and asp you tread, You tramp young lion and dragon.
91.14: Because in Me he has delighted, I also deliver him--I set him on high, Because he has known My name.
91.15: He does call Me, and I answer him, I am with him in distress, I deliver him, and honour him.
91.16: With length of days I satisfy him, And I cause him to look on My salvation!

92.1: A Psalm. --A Song for the sabbath-day. Good to give thanks to Jehovah, And to sing praises to Your name, O Most High,
92.2: To declare in the morning Your kindness, And Your faithfulness in the nights.
92.3: On ten strings and on psaltery, On higgaion, with harp.
92.4: For You have caused me to rejoice, O Jehovah, in Your work, Concerning the works of Your hands I sing.
92.5: How great have been Your works, O Jehovah, Very deep have been Your thoughts.
92.6: A brutish man does not know, And a fool understands not this; --
92.7: When the wicked flourish as a herb, And blossom do all workers of iniquity--For their being destroyed for ever and ever!
92.8: And You are high to the age, O Jehovah.
92.9: For, indeed, Your enemies, O Jehovah, For, indeed, Your enemies, do perish, Separate themselves do all workers of iniquity.
92.10: And You exalt as a reem my horn, I have been anointed with fresh oil.
92.11: And my eye looks on my enemies, Of those rising up against me, The evil doers, do my ears hear.
92.12: The righteous as a palm-tree flourishes, As a cedar in Lebanon he grows.
92.13: Those planted in the house of Jehovah, In the courts of our God do flourish.
92.14: Still they bring forth in old age, Fat and flourishing are they,
92.15: To declare that upright is Jehovah my rock, And there is no perverseness in Him!

93.1: Jehovah has reigned, Excellency He has put on, Jehovah put on strength, He girded Himself, Also--established is the world, unmoved.
93.2: Established is Your throne since then, From the age You are.
93.3: Floods have lifted up, O Jehovah, Floods have lifted up their voice, Floods lift up their breakers.
93.4: Than the voices of many mighty waters, Breakers of a sea, mighty on high is Jehovah,
93.5: Your testimonies have been very stedfast, To Your house comely is holiness, O Jehovah, for length of days!

94.1: God of vengeance--Jehovah! God of vengeance, shine forth.
94.2: Be lifted up, O Judge of the earth, Send back a recompence on the proud.
94.3: Till when do the wicked, O Jehovah? Till when do the wicked exult?
94.4: They utter--they speak an old saw, All working iniquity do boast themselves.
94.5: Your people, O Jehovah, they bruise, And Your inheritance they afflict.
94.6: Widow and sojourner they slay, And fatherless ones they murder.
94.7: And they say, `Jehovah does not see, And the God of Jacob does not consider.'
94.8: Consider, you brutish among the people, And you foolish, when do you act wisely?
94.9: He who plants the ear does He not hear? He who forms the eye does He not see?
94.10: He who is instructing nations, Does He not reprove? He who is teaching man knowledge is Jehovah.
94.11: He knows the thoughts of man, that they are vanity.
94.12: O the happiness of the man Whom You instruct, O Jah, And out of Your law teach him,
94.13: To give rest to him from days of evil, While a pit is digged for the wicked.
94.14: For Jehovah leaves not His people, And His inheritance forsakes not.
94.15: For to righteousness judgment turns back, And after it all the upright of heart,
94.16: Who rises up for me with evil doers? Who stations himself for me with workers of iniquity?
94.17: Unless Jehovah were a help to me, My soul had almost inhabited silence.
94.18: If I have said, `My foot has slipped,' Your kindness, O Jehovah, supports me.
94.19: In the abundance of my thoughts within me, Your comforts delight my soul.
94.20: Is a throne of mischief joined with You? A framer of perverseness by statute?
94.21: They decree against the soul of the righteous, And innocent blood declare wicked.
94.22: And Jehovah is for a high place to me, And my God is for a rock--my refuge,
94.23: And turns back on them their iniquity, And in their wickedness cuts them off; Jehovah our God does cut them off!

95.1: Come, we sing to Jehovah, We shout to the rock of our salvation.
95.2: We come before His face with thanksgiving, With psalms we shout to Him.
95.3: For a great God is Jehovah, And a great king over all gods.
95.4: In whose hand are the deep places of earth, And the strong places of hills are His.
95.5: Whose is the sea, and He made it, And His hands formed the dry land.
95.6: Come in, we bow ourselves, and we bend, We kneel before Jehovah our Maker.
95.7: For He is our God, and we the people of His pasture, And the flock of His hand, To-day, if to His voice you hearken,
95.8: Harden not your heart as in Meribah, As in the day of Massah in the wilderness,
95.9: Where your fathers have tried Me, Have proved Me, yes, have seen My work.
95.10: Forty years I am weary of the generation, And I say, `A people erring in heart--they! And they have not known My ways:'
95.11: Where I swore in My anger, `If they come in to My rest--!'

96.1: Sing to Jehovah a new song, Sing to Jehovah all the earth.
96.2: Sing to Jehovah, bless His name, Proclaim from day to day His salvation.
96.3: Declare among nations His honour, Among all the peoples His wonders.
96.4: For great is Jehovah, and praised greatly, Fearful He is over all gods.
96.5: For all the gods of the peoples are nought, And Jehovah made the heavens.
96.6: Honour and majesty are before Him, Strength and beauty in His sanctuary.
96.7: Ascribe to Jehovah, O families of the peoples, Ascribe to Jehovah honour and strength.
96.8: Ascribe to Jehovah the honour of His name, Lift up a present and come in to His courts.
96.9: Bow yourselves to Jehovah, In the honour of holiness, Be afraid of His presence, all the earth.
96.10: Say among nations, `Jehovah has reigned, Also--established is the world, unmoved, He judges the peoples in uprightness.'
96.11: The heavens joy, and the earth is joyful, The sea and its fulness roar.
96.12: The field exults, and all that is in it, Then sing do all trees of the forest,
96.13: Before Jehovah, for He has come, For He has come to judge the earth. He judges the world in righteousness, And the peoples in His faithfulness!

97.1: Jehovah has reigned, The earth is joyful, many isles rejoice.
97.2: Cloud and darkness are round about Him, Righteousness and judgment the basis of His throne.
97.3: Fire before Him goes, And burns round about His adversaries.
97.4: Lightened have His lightnings the world, The earth has seen, and is pained.
97.5: Hills, like wax, melted before Jehovah, Before the Lord of all the earth.
97.6: The heavens declared His righteousness, And all the peoples have seen His honour.
97.7: Ashamed are all servants of a graven image, Those boasting themselves in idols, Bow yourselves to him, all you gods.
97.8: Zion has heard and rejoices, And daughters of Judah are joyful, Because of Your judgments, O Jehovah.
97.9: For You, Jehovah, are Most High over all the earth, Greatly You have been exalted over all gods.
97.10: You who love Jehovah, hate evil, He is keeping the souls of His saints, From the hand of the wicked he delivers them.
97.11: Light is sown for the righteous, And for the upright of heart--joy.
97.12: Rejoice, you righteous, in Jehovah, And give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness!

98.1: A Psalm. Sing you to Jehovah a new song, For wonders He has done, Given salvation to Him has His right hand and His holy arm.
98.2: Jehovah has made known His salvation, Before the eyes of the nations, He has revealed His righteousness,
98.3: He has remembered His kindness, And His faithfulness to the house of Israel, All ends of earth have seen the salvation of our God.
98.4: Shout to Jehovah, all the earth, Break forth, and cry aloud, and sing.
98.5: Sing to Jehovah with harp, With harp, and voice of praise,
98.6: With trumpets, and voice of a cornet, Shout you before the king Jehovah.
98.7: Roar does the sea and its fulness, The world and the inhabitants in it.
98.8: Floods clap hand, together hills cry aloud,
98.9: Before Jehovah, For He has come to judge the earth, He judges the world in righteousness, And the people in uprightness!

99.1: Jehovah has reigned, peoples tremble, The Inhabitant of the cherubs, the earth shakes.
99.2: Jehovah in Zion is great, And high He is over all the peoples.
99.3: They praise Your name, `Great, and fearful, holy it is.'
99.4: And the strength of the king Has loved judgment, You--You have established uprightness; Judgment and righteousness in Jacob, You--You have done.
99.5: Exalt you Jehovah our God, And bow yourselves at His footstool, holy is He.
99.6: Moses and Aaron among His priests, And Samuel among those proclaiming His name. They are calling to Jehovah, And He does answer them.
99.7: In a pillar of cloud He speaks to them, They have kept His testimonies, And the statute He has given to them.
99.8: O Jehovah, our God, You have afflicted them, A God forgiving You have been to them, And taking vengeance on their actions.
99.9: Exalt you Jehovah our God, And bow yourselves at His holy hill, For holy is Jehovah our God!

100.1: A Psalm of Thanksgiving. Shout to Jehovah, all the earth.
100.2: Serve Jehovah with joy, come before him with singing.
100.3: Know that Jehovah He is God, He made us, and we are His, His people--and the flock of His pasture.
100.4: Enter you His gates with thanksgiving, His courts with praise, Give you thanks to Him, bless you His Name.
100.5: For good is Jehovah, to the age His kindness, And to generation and generation His faithfulness!

101.1: A Psalm of David. Kindness and judgment I sing, To You, O Jehovah, I sing praise.
101.2: I act wisely in a perfect way, When do You come in to me? I walk habitually in the integrity of my heart, In the midst of my house.
101.3: I set not before my eyes a worthless thing, The work of those turning aside I have hated, It adheres not to me.
101.4: A perverse heart turns aside from me, Wickedness I know not.
101.5: Whoever slanders in secret his neighbour, Him I cut off, The high of eyes and proud of heart, him I endure not.
101.6: My eyes are on the faithful of the land, To dwell with me, Whoever is walking in a perfect way, he serves me.
101.7: He dwells not in my house who is working deceit, Whoever is speaking lies Is not established before my eyes.
101.8: At morning I cut off all the wicked of the land, To cut off from the city of Jehovah All the workers of iniquity!

102.1: A Prayer of the afflicted when he is feeble, and before Jehovah pours out his plaint. O Jehovah, hear my prayer, yes, my cry to You comes.
102.2: Hide not You Your face from me, In a day of my adversity, Incline to me Your ear, In the day I call, haste, answer me.
102.3: For consumed in smoke have been my days, And my bones as a fire-brand have burned.
102.4: Smitten as the herb, and withered, is my heart, For I have forgotten to eat my bread.
102.5: From the voice of my sighing Has my bone cleaved to my flesh.
102.6: I have been like to a pelican of the wilderness, I have been as an owl of the dry places.
102.7: I have watched, and I am As a bird alone on the roof.
102.8: All the day my enemies reproached me, Those mad at me have sworn against me.
102.9: Because ashes as bread I have eaten, And my drink with weeping have mingled,
102.10: From Your indignation and Your wrath, For You have lifted me up, And do cast me down.
102.11: My days as a shadow are stretched out, And I--as the herb I am withered.
102.12: And You, O Jehovah, to the age abide, And Your memorial to all generations.
102.13: You--You rise--You pity Zion, For the time to favour her, For the appointed time has come.
102.14: For Your servants have been pleased with her stones, And her dust they favour.
102.15: And nations fear the name of Jehovah, And all kings of the earth Your honour,
102.16: For Jehovah has builded Zion, He has been seen in His honour,
102.17: He turned to the prayer of the destitute, And He has not despised their prayer.
102.18: This is written for a later generation, And the people created do praise Jah.
102.19: For He has looked From the high place of His sanctuary. Jehovah from heaven to earth looked attentively,
102.20: To hear the groan of the prisoner, To loose sons of death,
102.21: To declare in Zion the name of Jehovah, And His praise in Jerusalem,
102.22: In the peoples being gathered together, And the kingdoms--to serve Jehovah.
102.23: He has humbled in the way my power, He has shortened my days.
102.24: I say, `My God, take me not up in the midst of my days,' Through all generations are Yours years.
102.25: Beforetime the earth You did found, And the work of Your hands are the heavens.
102.26: They--They perish, and You remain, And all of them as a garment become old, As clothing You change them, And they are changed.
102.27: And You are the same, and Your years are not finished.
102.28: The sons of Your servants do continue, And their seed before You is established!

103.1: By David. Bless, O my soul, Jehovah, And all my inward parts--His Holy Name.
103.2: Bless, O my soul, Jehovah, And forget not all His benefits,
103.3: Who is forgiving all your iniquities, Who is healing all your diseases,
103.4: Who is redeeming from destruction your life, Who is crowning you--kindness and mercies,
103.5: Who is satisfying with good your desire, Renew itself as an eagle does your youth.
103.6: Jehovah is doing righteousness and judgments For all the oppressed.
103.7: He makes known His ways to Moses, To the sons of Israel His acts.
103.8: Merciful and gracious is Jehovah, Slow to anger, and abundant in mercy.
103.9: Not for ever does He strive, Nor to the age does He watch.
103.10: Not according to our sins has He done to us, Nor according to our iniquities Has He conferred benefits upon us.
103.11: For, as the height of the heavens is above the earth, His kindness has been mighty over those fearing Him.
103.12: As the distance of east from west He has put far from us our transgressions.
103.13: As a father has mercy on sons, Jehovah has mercy on those fearing Him.
103.14: For He has known our frame, Remembering that we are dust.
103.15: Mortal man! as grass are his days, As a flower of the field so he flourishes;
